hints.title: Coordinate Invariance
hints.text: Although numbers range up to 10^9, only at most three candidate values per number in nums can achieve the optimal maximum frequency.

hints.title: Candidate Collection
hints.text: Collect nums[i], nums[i] - k, and nums[i] + k for all i into a sorted set of candidate values.

hints.title: Fast Range Lookup
hints.text: Use binary search on sorted nums to determine exact count and reachable interval count in O(log n) time per candidate.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right

class Solution:
    def maxFrequency(self, nums: list[int], k: int, numOperations: int) -> int:
        nums.sort()
        candidates = set()
        for x in nums:
            candidates.add(x)
            candidates.add(x - k)
            candidates.add(x + k)
            
        ans = 0
        for v in candidates:
            left = bisect_left(nums, v - k)
            right = bisect_right(nums, v + k)
            total_in_range = right - left
            exact = bisect_right(nums, v) - bisect_left(nums, v)
            achievable = exact + min(numOperations, total_in_range - exact)
            if achievable > ans:
                ans = achievable
                
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Sorting followed by binary search boundary evaluation over at most 3n unique candidate points.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Values up to 10^9 prevent using frequency buckets or direct difference arrays.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) space for candidate set and sorted array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizes interval intersection candidate testing with coordinate reduction and logarithmic range queries.
